headline: Directing AI Video by Writing It Like Code
lede: A structured JSON prompt circulating among AI video enthusiasts offers an unusually precise creative brief for generating a cinematic product ad — complete with camera moves, transition logic, and an audio spec. The subject is not the Apple Watch itself but a technique: using the rigid hierarchy of JSON to force AI video models toward coherent, continuous-shot filmmaking. What reads like a developer's config file is, in practice, a director's shot list.
body:
The prompt, shared as item four in a series by @EHuanglu, decomposes a thirty-second product showcase into seven discrete JSON objects — each one naming a shot type, a camera behaviour, and a description of what should appear on screen. The sequence follows a familiar luxury-goods grammar: logo dissolved into particles, particles condensed into product, product revealed in a stripped-back showroom, camera pulling back to frame the full composition. What makes the prompt notable is not the aesthetic but the **structure**. Free-form text instructions to AI video generators tend to drift — the model interpolates, contradicts itself, cuts when you wanted a transition. JSON enforces an explicit sequence, making it harder for the model to skip or reorder beats.

The prompt's hardest constraint is its insistence on continuity. Every section repeats some variation of "without any cut" or "continuous motion, no cut," attempting to coerce the generator into producing a single unbroken take rather than a montage of independently rendered clips stitched together in post. Current AI video tools — including Veo 3 (made by Alphabet (GOOGL)), Kling AI (developed by Kuaishou Technology (1024.HK)), and Runway — struggle with exactly this requirement. Physical consistency across an extended shot, especially one involving particle metamorphosis and environmental worldbuilding, remains at the frontier of what these systems can reliably produce. The prompt is aspirational as much as practical.

The cinematographic vocabulary is borrowed largely from real-time 3D rendering and product visualisation rather than live-action filmmaking: *volumetric lighting* (light rendered as a participating medium, creating visible rays and atmospheric depth), macro camera paths, brushed-aluminium surfaces with underglow. This is the visual language of a high-end CGI commercial, and it points to where AI video is heading — not replacing documentary or drama first, but eating into the product-visualisation and motion-graphics budgets that studios and agencies charge dearly for.

The broader trend here is *JSON prompting* as a discipline in its own right. As AI video models improve, the quality ceiling shifts from the model's raw capability to the quality of the creative brief fed into it. Users who can articulate shot logic, lighting intent, and transition grammar in machine-readable form gain a reproducibility advantage: the same JSON skeleton can be repurposed for any product by swapping a handful of values. What is being shared is less a prompt than a reusable template — a modest but genuine piece of prompting infrastructure.

concepts.definition: The practice of writing AI model instructions in JSON format rather than free-form prose. JSON's key-value hierarchy forces the prompter to decompose a creative task into explicit, ordered fields — shot type, camera move, description — giving the model a more deterministic skeleton to follow. Popular with AI video tools where sequence and continuity matter.

A rendering technique that simulates light interacting with particles or haze in the air, creating visible shafts, rays, or atmospheric glow. Unlike surface-only lighting, it gives a scene depth and physical presence. Common in CGI product visualisation and game engines; computationally expensive in traditional pipelines but increasingly generated by AI video models as a stylistic shorthand.

A filmmaking instruction requiring the camera to move through a sequence without any editorial cut or hard transition. In AI video generation, this is technically demanding because it forces the model to maintain spatial and physical consistency across the full duration rather than independently rendering clips that are later stitched together.

A visual-effects technique where an object dissolves into a cloud of small particles which then reform into a different shape — used here to transition seamlessly from a brand logo to the physical product. Associated with CGI and motion graphics; difficult for current AI video models to execute with geometric precision across a continuous take.

The use of large generative models to produce video clips from text or structured prompts, without traditional filming or animation. Models such as Veo 3, Kling AI, and Runway take a prompt and output seconds-to-minutes of video. Output quality and physical consistency vary significantly across tools and prompt styles.

thread_summary: The tweet is item four in a numbered series from @EHuanglu sharing structured AI video prompts. The series appears to catalogue reusable JSON-formatted prompt templates for generating cinematic product advertisements using AI video tools.
